description:
Godot 4 glue for Noodloft components: an ILogger over GD.Print/PushWarning/PushError, and
            an ISaveStore over user:// via Godot's own FileAccess, so saves work on Android and web
            where there is no real filesystem path.

            The nodes and resources are NOT in this package. Godot keys C# script types to a res://
            path, which a type inside a DLL does not have, so they ship as addon source instead.
releaseNotes:
Everything here came out of running the addon in a real Godot project for the first time. Two of
the three stopped it working at all.

### Fixed

- **The addon source did not compile in a Godot project at all.** Every file relied on implicit
  usings and an enabled nullable context, and `Godot.NET.Sdk` turns on neither — but the compile-check
  project in this repo turned on both, so the check passed while a real consumer's build failed on 40
  errors. The symptom is indirect and nothing like the cause: a failed build means no `[GlobalClass]`
  is registered, so custom resources cannot be assigned in the inspector, and any `.tres` saved in
  that state is a plain `Godot.Resource` — which surfaces later as
  `InvalidCastException: Unable to cast object of type 'Godot.Resource'`. Every file under `addons/`
  now carries its own `using` directives and `#nullable enable`, and the compile-check project sets
  `ImplicitUsings=disable` and `Nullable=disable` so it fails the same way a consumer's project would.

  **Any `.tres` or scene saved while this was broken has to be recreated** — the resource stored in
  it has no script attached, and no amount of rebuilding will give it one.

- **The Godot package would not load in the engine version it claims to support.**
  `Noodloft.Components.Games.Godot` referenced `GodotSharp` as `4.*`, which NuGet floats to whatever
  is newest on the build machine — so the published DLL was compiled against GodotSharp 4.7.1 while
  the addon and the documentation both name 4.4 as the floor. GodotSharp bumps its AssemblyVersion
  every release (4.4.0 is `4.4.0.0`, 4.7.1 is `4.7.1.0`), and .NET's default load context satisfies a
  reference with a *higher* version but never a lower one. In a Godot 4.4 project the reference could
  not resolve, so the project assembly failed to load and every script in it failed with it — whose
  only visible symptom is the editor reporting `Unable to load addon script from path:
  'res://addons/noodloft.components/NoodloftComponentsPlugin.cs'` and disabling the plugin. Now pinned
  to `[4.4.0]`, so the shipped assembly binds to the floor and loads in every supported engine.

### Changed

- **The autoload is now `NoodloftSaveManager`, not `SaveManager`.** An autoload occupies a global name
  in every script in the project, and `SaveManager` is a name a game is likely to want for its own.
  Breaking: rename the autoload in Project Settings, or disable and re-enable the plugin, and update
  any `GetNode("/root/SaveManager")` to `/root/NoodloftSaveManager`.
